title: List membership of Sanitizer name in Sanitizer API
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The WICG version of Sanitizer API (https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api) specifies that:

> For the canonicalized element and attribute name lists used in this spec, list membership is based on matching both "name" and "namespace" entries
> https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/#alg-support

Additionally, there are some supporting algorithms supporting this concept:

- contains: https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/#sanitizerconfig-contains
- remove: https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/#sanitizerconfig-remove
- add: https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/#sanitizerconfig-add
- has duplicates: https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/#sanitizerconfig-has-duplicates

However, these seem to be removed in the version merged into HTML Standard, and use the general algorithms from Infra Standard instead:

- contains: https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain
- remove: https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove
- append: https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append
- has duplicates: https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-has-duplicates

I think this could lead to some problems.

For example, in the [`allowElement(element)`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#dom-sanitizer-allowelement) method, the method argument *element* is a `SanitizerElementWithAttributes`, and it is canonicalized in step 3. Therefore, either *element["attributes"]* or *element["removeAttributes"]* exists. Then, step 4.1 tries to remove *element* from *configuration["replaceWithChildrenElements"]*, which is a list of `SanitizerElement` and each entry must not have *"attributes"* or *"removeAttributes"* field. That means *element* must not be equal to any entry in *configuration["replaceWithChildrenElements"]*, and thus nothing is removed.

Another example is in the detection of duplicates when determining whether a canonical `SanitizerConfig` config is valid. Assume *config["elements"]* contains these two `SanitizerElementWithAttributes`:
- `{name: "input", attributes: [{name: "type"}]}`
- `{name: "input", attributes: [{name: "value"}]}`

In step 8.1 of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#dom-sanitizerconfig-valid, under the **has duplicates** algorithm from Infra Standard, they are not considered as duplicates. On the other hand, in step 8.1 of https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/#sanitizerconfig-valid, under the [custom **has duplicates** algorithm](https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/#sanitizerconfig-has-duplicates), they are considered as duplicates.

cc. @noamr
